natalie: ran the 1h continuous-batching profile against live p95 traffic, saw a surprising decode-rate skew. short prompts (~<32 tokens) have much higher decode tokens/sec and are getting grouped into mixed batches -> wrong kernel chosen, KV miss rate spikes :confused:
kevin: can you paste the profiler output? which kernel mismatch do we see?
jordan: +1 need the sample. are we seeing more small-token fast-decode requests being paired with long-slow ones?
natalie: yes. here's the trimmed trace (from perf-agent):
```
# sample from 2923456720
batch_size=8
requests: [r1(len=18,dr=420 t/s), r2(len=600,dr=60 t/s), r3(len=22,dr=410 t/s), ...]
chosen_kernel: matmul-mixed-fp16-optim
expected_kernel_short: fast-slice-attn
kv_cache_hits: 0.12
kv_prefetch: off
latency_p50=38ms p95=220ms p99=520ms
token_throughput_variance=4.8x
```
liam: ouch, that explains the latency tail. kernel selection logic is using batch-avg decode rate and weighted length; that avg is getting pulled by the long ones so we pick the slower code path for the whole batch.
kevin: I think classifier thresholds for length buckets are too coarse. We currently use buckets [0-64,65-256,>256]. The decode-rate distribution suggests we need a short-fast bucket at [0-32] and a separate mid-short [33-128].
jordan: also kv behavior: small prompts are cold-starting KV caches because we don't prefetch for <64 tokens. That increases miss rate and further slows those requests when they're paired with long ones.
natalie: proposal: update workload classifier to use a 4-bucket split: [0-32,33-128,129-512,>512] and add decode-rate-aware token budget targets per bucket. Token budgets: short-fast -> 16*batch_size cap, mid-short -> 12*batch_size, others -> current defaults.
liam: +1. And add a quick heuristic: if batch contains >30% requests from the short-fast bucket, favor fast-slice-attn kernel and cap max batch size for that batch to avoid too much mixing.
kevin: sounds good. Also enable KV-prefetch for short prompts with a small window (prefetch up to 64 tokens) to reduce miss penalty. Testable in canary.
jordan: can we simulate impact on cost? shorter kernel path uses different CUDA kernels with higher efficiency per-token; batching differently will change throughput. I can run a cost sim with the new buckets.
perf-bot: perf-run queued: cbv-sim-2923456789 (configs: 4-bucket-classifier, kv-prefetch-short=true, short-kernel-favor=true). ETA 2h.
natalie: great. for the canary plan: 1) deploy classifier change on 5% nodes 2) enable kv-prefetch short 3) apply kernel-favor rule 4) monitor p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, tokens_per_sec, avg_kernel_util.
kevin: add a guard: if p99 increases by >10% or cost per token increases >8% revert.
liam: i'll instrument an additional metric: batch_composition.short_percent to alert when mixed batches exceed 40%.
jordan: i'll run the cost + quality sim now and post numbers in this thread.
natalie: thanks. short checklist: update classifier thresholds in repo (runtime/batcher/classifier.py), add unit tests for boundary cases, add prefetch flag toggle in kv_manager, create canary rollout PR. tagging @kevin @liam for reviews. :white_check_mark:
kevin: will review PR tomorrow morning.
perf-bot: perf-run completed: cbv-sim-2923456789 results uploaded to /perf/runs/2923456789. Summary: projected p95 latency -12%, p99 -5%, kv_hit_rate +18% for short bucket, estimated cost/token -3.4%.
natalie: love those numbers. let's proceed with canary on staging this afternoon and monitor.
jordan: posting sim charts now: https://internal/perf/runs/2923456789/charts (look at batch_composition and kernel_swap_rate).
liam: noted. will set alert and watch the first 2h after canary.
natalie: thanks team — follow-ups: PR link + canary run ID in #eng-releases when deployed.
kevin: quick note: when we roll out, let's also log per-batch kernel decision reason to help future tuning (short_bucket_bias, avg_decode_rate, kv_prefetch_flag). small logging change but huge debugging win.
natalie: agreed. adding to PR. :rocket:
